svg.title: Every centimetre of cover costs read range — UHF read range vs concrete cover depth
svg.desc: Horizontal bar chart of handheld UHF read range versus concrete cover depth for a cast-in RFID tag, on a scale from zero at the element surface to the 1.0 metre top of the read window, with a dashed gridline at the 0.3 metre floor. Row one: at 25 to 50 millimetres of cover, the recommended ACI 301 placement band, the bar runs toward 1.0 metres at the surface. Row two: at 50 to 75 millimetres, the deep placement band, the bar lands inside the 0.3 to 1.0 metre window and surface reads should be planned. Row three: from 75 millimetres to the 10 centimetre read-through ceiling, range approaches 0.3 metres with the reader held against the surface. Row four, the failure state in red: beyond 10 centimetres of cover there is no reliable UHF read — the tag placement must move, not the reader. Footnotes: attenuation also rises with rebar density, limestone aggregate is more RF-transparent than granite, and all bands come from the page's specification table.
svg.text: UHF READ RANGE VS CONCRETE COVER DEPTH
Every centimetre of cover costs read range
The handheld window is 0.3–1.0 m through 5–10 cm of cured cover — placement depth decides where in it you land
inside the 0.3–1.0 m window — plan surface reads
no reliable UHF read — move the tag, not the reader
Attenuation also rises with rebar density — and aggregate matters: limestone is more RF-transparent than granite.
Bands and window per this page's specification table: 25–75 mm typical placement (25–50 mm optimal) · 5–10 cm read-through · 0.3–1.0 m handheld window.
